title: Thomas Tuchel casts doubt on Phil Foden’s England World Cup squad chances
content:
England head coach Thomas Tuchel has cast doubt on Phil Foden’s chances of being selected for the World Cup after the Manchester City playmaker’s displays against Uruguay and Japan.

Foden was given a chance to impress by Tuchel, who started the 25-year-old in both matches, but he struggled to make an impact in either friendly and was twice replaced before the hour mark.

Tuchel is required to submit his final World Cup squad on May 30 and has warned Foden that there are no guarantees that his name will be on the 26-man list.

“He tried everything,” Tuchel, taking a sharp intake of breath before responding, told reporters when asked if Foden had taken his chance in the Uruguay draw and Japan defeat.

“I would say he was excellent in camp but, yeah, he struggles to show it on the pitch.

“Obviously, he didn’t have a lot of minutes for City recently. Then he came to camp with the brightest smile and was so good in training and I thought he will just surprise us and will play with the same verve and excitement but, yeah, he struggles to have the full impact.”

Foden, who played as a false nine in the defeat by Japan at Wembley Stadium on Tuesday night, has not scored for the national team since October 2022, a run that now extends to 22 matches.

Tuchel experimenting with Foden in place of the injured Harry Kane did not work, and the City man had the fewest touches of any starting England player, prompting the German to cast doubt on his World Cup prospects.

“I can, but the question would be if we will,” Tuchel added when asked if he would take an underperforming player to North America. “It’s not a guarantee that he will come.”

Although England are regarded as one of the favourites to win the World Cup, Tuchel has routinely downplayed that tag.

They begin the tournament in Dallas against Croatia on June 17, before playing Ghana in Boston on June 23 and Panama in New Jersey to round off the group stage on June 27.

And despite the below-par friendly performances, Tuchel, asked if it had dampened expectations ahead of the summer, said he is still optimistic.

“Like I said, we will not let go of our dream, not let go of the question ‘Why not?’,” he added. “Now the most important thing is that the players reintegrate with their clubs, have a good end to the season, and then we have them in pre-camp and prepare them properly and take steps from there.”
